name: Amazon Security Lake CloudTrail (OCSF)
description: AWS CloudTrail management events as Amazon Security Lake normalizes them to OCSF API Activity (class_uid 6003), pulled by the Splunk Add-on for AWS's Security Lake input (SQS-based S3, Parquet, s3_file_decoder=AmazonSecurityLake).
source: The OCSF 1.3.0 schema (API Activity class and its Actor, API, Cloud, Metadata, Network Endpoint, Observable, Resource Details, Session, User, Identity Provider, HTTP Request and Authorization Result objects) for the OCSF-shaped fields; the AWS CloudTrail user guide's record-contents and userIdentity pages for the fields CloudTrail keeps under unmapped; the Splunk Add-on for AWS docs for the sourcetype and input. Checked against a metadata-only field list captured from a dev Splunk instance (no CloudTrail sample data available for aws:asl).

feed.label: Amazon Security Lake CloudTrail
feed.description: AWS CloudTrail activity normalized to OCSF by Amazon Security Lake: who called which API, on what resource, from where, and whether it succeeded.

asl_account_id.label: AWS account id
asl_account_id.description: The AWS account the event or the resource it names belongs to.

ocsf_activity.label: Activity
ocsf_activity.description: The normalized CRUD activity the API call performed, as an id and its caption.

ocsf_category.label: Category
ocsf_category.description: The event's OCSF category: for aws:asl this is always Application Activity (category_uid 6).

ocsf_class.label: Class
ocsf_class.description: The event's OCSF class: for aws:asl this is always API Activity (class_uid 6003), OCSF's class for CRUD API calls such as AWS CloudTrail.

ocsf_type.label: Type
ocsf_type.description: The derived event type: type_uid = class_uid * 100 + activity_id, type_name joins class_name and activity_name with a colon.

ocsf_severity.label: Severity
ocsf_severity.description: The event's normalized severity, as an id and its caption.

ocsf_status.label: Status
ocsf_status.description: The event status, normalized to the caption of the (unobserved) status_id value: whether the API call succeeded.

event_time.label: Event time
event_time.description: The normalized event occurrence time, as epoch (time) and ISO datetime (time_dt).

idp_name.label: Identity provider name
idp_name.description: The name of the identity provider used, when the caller authenticated through one.

invoked_by.label: Invoked by
invoked_by.description: The name of the AWS service that invoked the activity, when a service (not a person) made the call.

session_created_time.label: Session created time
session_created_time.description: The time the session's temporary credentials were created, not the event time.

session_is_mfa.label: Session MFA used
session_is_mfa.description: Whether multi-factor authentication was used to establish the session.

session_issuer.label: Session issuer
session_issuer.description: The identifier of the entity that issued the session (the role or user session context came from).

credential_uid.label: Credential id
credential_uid.description: The id of the credential used, for example an AWS access key id.

actor_user_name.label: Actor user name
actor_user_name.description: The human-readable name of the user or role that made the call.

actor_user_type.label: Actor user type
actor_user_type.description: The type of identity that made the call: OCSF's caption of the CloudTrail userIdentity.type value (Root, IAMUser, AssumedRole, Role, FederatedUser, Directory, AWSAccount, AWSService, IdentityCenterUser or Unknown).

actor_user_uid.label: Actor user id
actor_user_uid.description: The stable identifier of the user or role that made the call; for CloudTrail-sourced events this is the caller's ARN or principal id.

actor_user_uid_alt.label: Actor user alternate id
actor_user_uid_alt.description: An alternate identifier for the same user or role.

session_uid.label: Session id
session_uid.description: The unique identifier of the session; uid_alt carries the session's ARN form for an assumed role, for example arn:aws:sts::123344444444:assumed-role/Admin/example-session.

api_operation.label: API operation
api_operation.description: The verb or operation the request performed; for CloudTrail-sourced events this is the eventName.

api_request_data.label: API request data
api_request_data.description: The request's own parameters, nested as reported by the source.

api_request_uid.label: API request id
api_request_uid.description: The id assigned to the request by the service that handled it.

api_response_data.label: API response data
api_response_data.description: The response's own elements, nested as reported by the source.

api_response_error.label: API response error
api_response_error.description: The service error code, when the call failed.

api_response_message.label: API response message
api_response_message.description: The description of the event, as OCSF's response.message reports it; carries the failure text when the API call did not succeed.

api_service_name.label: API service name
api_service_name.description: The AWS service the call was made to.

api_version.label: API version
api_version.description: The version of the API the call used.

asl_version.label: ASL schema version
asl_version.description: Amazon Security Lake's own mapping/schema version for the record, distinct from metadata.version (the OCSF schema version).

cloud_provider.label: Cloud provider
cloud_provider.description: The cloud provider name; always AWS for this sourcetype.

cloud_region.label: Cloud region
cloud_region.description: The AWS region the call was made in.

endpoint_svc_name.label: Destination service name
endpoint_svc_name.description: The service name on the destination side of a service-to-service call.

http_user_agent.label: HTTP user agent
http_user_agent.description: The client's self-reported user agent string on the underlying HTTP request.

metadata_event_code.label: Event code
metadata_event_code.description: The event id or code the source product uses to describe the event.

metadata_product_feature.label: Product feature name
metadata_product_feature.description: The name of the product feature that reported the event.

metadata_product_name.label: Product name
metadata_product_name.description: The name of the product that reported the event.

metadata_product_vendor.label: Product vendor name
metadata_product_vendor.description: The vendor of the product that reported the event.

metadata_product_version.label: Product version
metadata_product_version.description: The version of the product that reported the event.

metadata_profiles.label: OCSF profiles
metadata_profiles.description: The list of OCSF profiles used to build the event.

metadata_uid.label: Event id
metadata_uid.description: The logging system's own unique id for the event instance; for CloudTrail-sourced events this is the CloudTrail eventID GUID.

metadata_version.label: OCSF schema version
metadata_version.description: The version of the OCSF schema the event was built against.

observable_name.label: Observable name
observable_name.description: The event field the observable points to, for example file.name.

observable_type.label: Observable type
observable_type.description: The kind of value the observable carries, as an id and its caption (Hostname, IP Address, Resource UID, User Credential ID and others).

observable_value.label: Observable value
observable_value.description: The value itself; its meaning depends on the sibling type.

policy_uid.label: Policy id
policy_uid.description: The id of an IAM policy applicable to the authorization decision, when one is reported.

resources_raw.label: Resources
resources_raw.description: The list of resources the activity affected, nested as reported by the source.

resources_type.label: Resource type
resources_type.description: The resource's type as reported by the event source, for example AWS::IAM::Role.

resources_uid.label: Resource id
resources_uid.description: The unique identifier of the resource, typically its ARN.

src_domain.label: Source domain
src_domain.description: The domain name of the request's source endpoint.

src_ip.label: Source IP
src_ip.description: The IP address the request came from.

src_endpoint_uid.label: Source endpoint id
src_endpoint_uid.description: The unique identifier of the source endpoint.

unmapped_addl_auth_method.label: Additional data: authentication method
unmapped_addl_auth_method.description: A CloudTrail additionalEventData key preserved unmapped; AWS documents additionalEventData's content as service- and event-specific and variable, and does not itself define AuthenticationMethod on the record-contents page.

unmapped_addl_cipher_suite.label: Additional data: cipher suite
unmapped_addl_cipher_suite.description: A CloudTrail additionalEventData key preserved unmapped; content is service- and event-specific.

unmapped_addl_signature_version.label: Additional data: signature version
unmapped_addl_signature_version.description: A CloudTrail additionalEventData key preserved unmapped; content is service- and event-specific.

unmapped_addl_bytes_in.label: Additional data: bytes transferred in
unmapped_addl_bytes_in.description: A CloudTrail additionalEventData key preserved unmapped; content is service- and event-specific.

unmapped_addl_bytes_out.label: Additional data: bytes transferred out
unmapped_addl_bytes_out.description: A CloudTrail additionalEventData key preserved unmapped; content is service- and event-specific.

unmapped_addl_amz_id2.label: Additional data: x-amz-id-2
unmapped_addl_amz_id2.description: An S3 request trace id. AWS's record-contents page documents this same field name under responseElements: 'Both x-amz-request-id and x-amz-id-2 contain information that helps you trace a request with Support.' It is preserved here under additionalEventData rather than responseElements.

unmapped_management_event.label: Management event flag
unmapped_management_event.description: Whether the event is a management event, per CloudTrail's own managementEvent field.

unmapped_read_only.label: Read-only operation flag
unmapped_read_only.description: Whether the operation is read-only, per CloudTrail's own readOnly field.

unmapped_recipient_account_id.label: Recipient account id
unmapped_recipient_account_id.description: The account that received the CloudTrail event; can differ from the actor's account in cross-account resource access.

unmapped_session_cred_console.label: Console session credential flag
unmapped_session_cred_console.description: Whether the API call's credentials originated from an AWS Management Console session, per CloudTrail's own sessionCredentialFromConsole field.

unmapped_tls_cipher_suite.label: TLS cipher suite
unmapped_tls_cipher_suite.description: The cipher suite used for the underlying TLS connection, per CloudTrail's own tlsDetails.cipherSuite.

unmapped_tls_host_header.label: TLS client-provided host header
unmapped_tls_host_header.description: The client-provided host name used in the API call, typically the service endpoint's FQDN, per CloudTrail's own tlsDetails.clientProvidedHostHeader.

unmapped_tls_version.label: TLS version
unmapped_tls_version.description: The TLS version of the request, per CloudTrail's own tlsDetails.tlsVersion.

unmapped_session_issuer_account.label: Session issuer account id
unmapped_session_issuer_account.description: The account that owns the role or user used to obtain the session's temporary credentials, per CloudTrail's own userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.accountId.

unmapped_session_issuer_principal.label: Session issuer principal id
unmapped_session_issuer_principal.description: The internal id of the role or user used to obtain the session's credentials; not the id of the session itself.

unmapped_session_issuer_type.label: Session issuer type
unmapped_session_issuer_type.description: The type of identity that issued the session's credentials (Root, IAMUser or Role).

unmapped_session_issuer_username.label: Session issuer user name
unmapped_session_issuer_username.description: The friendly name of the role or user that issued the session's credentials.

aws:asl.description: AWS API dataset data collected from Amazon Security Lake by the Splunk Add-on for AWS (SQS-Based S3 input, s3_file_decoder=AmazonSecurityLake, Apache Parquet source files). Each event is one OCSF API Activity record: the CloudTrail management event as Security Lake maps it, with fields CloudTrail itself defines but OCSF does not map kept verbatim under unmapped.
aws:asl.note: No sample dataset ships with this pack for this container: no vendor-published worked sample was found. Column names below are read from a field list captured from a live Splunk instance (metadata only, no event values); every value and example in this pack's dictionary is read from a vendor documentation page, not from a sample or a live event.

bindings.note: Top-level convenience column; not itself in OCSF's API Activity class field list, presumed a Security Lake or add-on flattening.
actor.user.account is the User object's Account sub-object; its uid is the AWS account id.
Top-level duplicate of actor.session.is_mfa; not in the class's own field list.
Resource Details' owner is a User object; owner.account.uid is that user's account id.
Top-level column, not in the class's own field list; presumed to mirror actor.user.credential_uid or a session-scoped credential_uid not otherwise observed.

asl_id_lookalike.text: aws:asl carries several same-shaped identifiers that are not interchangeable: actor.user.uid (the caller's ARN or principal id), actor.user.uid_alt, metadata.uid (a CloudTrail-assigned event GUID), resources.uid (a resource ARN), unmapped.userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.principalId (the role that issued the session, not the session itself) and actor.user.credential_uid (an access key id). Two of these can be the same string shape (an ARN or a 21-character AKIA/AROA id) while naming different entities; do not treat any pair as interchangeable without checking the field.

asl_flattened_top_level.text: session.uid, session.uid_alt, session.issuer, session.credential_uid and user.name, user.uid, user.uid_alt appear at the top level of aws:asl events, but OCSF's API Activity class (schema.ocsf.io/1.3.0/classes/api_activity, read 2026-09-19) nests session and user only under actor (actor.session.*, actor.user.*); no top-level session or user field is in that page's own field list. These top-level columns are presumed a Security Lake or Splunk add-on flattening of the actor sub-object, not confirmed against the add-on's own source; actor.session.* and actor.user.* are the citable path.

asl_time_lookalike.text: time/time_dt is the OCSF-normalized event occurrence time (schema.ocsf.io/1.3.0/classes/api_activity: 'The normalized event occurrence time...'). actor.session.created_time_dt is a different time: when the session's temporary credentials were issued, which can be hours before the API call the event records. Do not use created_time_dt as the event time.

asl_recipient_vs_actor_account.text: unmapped.recipientAccountId can differ from accountid / actor.user.account.uid in cross-account resource access: AWS's own record-contents page states 'The recipientAccountID may be different from the CloudTrail userIdentity element accountId. This can occur in cross-account resource access.' (read 2026-09-19). Do not assume the two name the same account.
